text: [“] And now they laugh at me, the fewer in days than I, whose fathers I disdained to put with the dogs of my flock.
Indeed, the strength of their hands, what [is it] to me? Upon them vigor has perished,
in poverty and in harsh hunger, ones gnawing the dry ground by night, [in] ruin and desolation.
They [are] plucking mallow among the brush, and the root of the broom tree is their bread.
From the midst of people they are driven out; they shout at them as [at] a thief.
On the slope of wadis [they are] to dwell, in holes of the dust and rocks.
Among the shrubs they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.
Sons of a fool, even sons without a name, they were scourged from the land.
And now I have become their song, and I have become a byword among them.
They abhor me [and] keep far from me; and from my face they do not withhold spit.
For my bowstring he has loosed and afflicted me, and they have cast [off] the bridle before me.
On the right a brood arises; they push away my feet, and they build up against me the ways of destruction.
They break up my path; they advance my calamity, with no one helping them.
As a wide breach they come; amid the ruin they roll on.
Terrors are turned over upon me; like the wind it pursues my honor, and like a cloud my deliverance has passed away.
And now within me my soul is poured out; days of affliction seize me.
Night pierces my bones from upon me, and my gnawing pains will not lie down.
With abundance of strength He grasps my garment; by the collar of my tunic He seizes me.
He has cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to You, but You do not answer me; I stand up, and You gaze at me.
You have turned to [be] cruel toward me; with the strength of Your hand You oppose me.
You lift me up to the wind and make me ride [it], You toss me about in the storm.
For I know [that] You will bring me [to] death, and [to] the house of appointment to all the living.
Surely one does not stretch out a hand against the oppressed, when in his ruin he cries out to [him].
If not did I weep for the harshness of day, [while] my soul grieved for the needy one?
And, I hoped for good, and evil came; and I waited for light, and darkness came.
My bowels have boiled and they do not rest; days of affliction confront me.
I go about darkened, not by the sun; I rise up in the assembly [and] cry out.
I have become a brother to jackals, and a companion to the daughters of the ostrich.
My skin turns black and falls from me, and my bone burns with heat.
And my harp is changed to mourning, and my flute to the voice of weeping.
